speaker: Tamara W. Runia
role: First Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency
title: The Sculpting of Our Souls
summary: Sister Runia teaches that hard experience is how God shapes us to become like Him, so trials are not a detour from the path but give it purpose. She tells of her son Ryan's sudden death, her grandson Jaac's Lego talk about trusting the designer, and her brother's sculpting class where a master's hand carved what his could not. She asks listeners to choose Christ, trust Him without understanding everything, and invite Him to do the carving.

audience.who: Anyone in grief or hardship they cannot fix; all members

findings.quote: Doctrine and Covenants 122:7
Galatians 3:27
Helaman 5:12
1 John 3:2

“Truly [God] loves us, and because He loves us, He neither compels nor abandons us. Rather He helps and guides us” (D. Todd Christofferson, “Free Forever, to Act for Themselves,” Liahona, Nov. 2014, 17). “In mortality, we can ‘come boldly’ to the Savior and receive compassion, healing, and help. Even while we suffer inexplicably, God can bless us in simple, ordinary, and significant ways. As we learn to recognize these blessings, our trust in God will increase” (Dale G. Renlund, “Infuriating Unfairness,” Liahona, May 2021, 43). See also Adam S. Miller, Letters to a Young Mormon (2014), 17–23.
findings.ref: Free Forever, to Act for Themselves
findings.note: Cites Elders Christofferson and Renlund on God's love and help in suffering, plus Adam S. Miller

detail.who: D. Todd Christofferson; Dale G. Renlund; Adam S. Miller

findings.quote: See Neal A. Maxwell, “Plow in Hope,” Liahona, July 2001, 72–74.
findings.note: Cites Elder Neal A. Maxwell

findings.quote: If there’s a knot in a shoelace or a necklace, it’s my job to untangle it.
findings.note: Opening self-portrait as a fixer; sets up what she cannot fix

detail.carries: our urge to fix things, and the limits of it

findings.quote: Thirteen years ago our oldest son, Ryan, woke up on a Monday morning, kissed his wife and four young children goodbye, and left for work.
findings.note: Her son's sudden death from an undetected heart condition

detail.about: son Ryan dies suddenly, the day before his daughter's birthday

findings.quote: our oldest son, Ryan
his two-year-old daughter Piper’s birthday
Let’s focus on a scripture that has changed the lens through which I view my life.
findings.note: A scripture as a new lens for seeing life

detail.carries: scripture changes how we see our trials

findings.quote: The setting is a jail cell, where Joseph Smith is pleading with God for a reprieve—for a break from his circumstance.
findings.note: Joseph Smith in Liberty Jail

detail.about: Joseph Smith pleads for relief in jail and is told experience is for his good

findings.quote: Instead, he was told, “All these things shall give thee experience, and shall be for thy good.”
findings.note: The Lord's voice to Joseph Smith in D&C 122

findings.quote: I’ve often wondered if the Prophet had any idea when he received this revelation what these words would mean to so many of us now
We studied it there, and we’re living it here, in this laboratory of life.
findings.note: Premortal classroom versus mortal laboratory

detail.carries: lessons learned in theory before birth are learned by experience here

findings.quote: C. S. Lewis explained, “God intends to give us what we need, not what we now think we want.”
I grew up hearing things like “If you keep the commandments, you’ll be blessed.
findings.note: Familiar gospel sayings from her upbringing

detail.who: common sayings she grew up hearing

findings.quote: Follow the Word of Wisdom, and you’ll have health and protection.” True promises, right?
findings.note: Three if-then promises she took as a shield from trials

items: pay tithing, windows of heaven open
keep the Word of Wisdom, health and protection
detail.purpose: promises she grew up expecting would keep hardship away

findings.quote: So the gospel felt like a big umbrella I could hold over my head to keep the rain from falling on me.
findings.note: The umbrella is the mistaken view she corrects

detail.carries: the false idea that the gospel keeps trials away

findings.quote: But I’ve learned from experience that we’re all going to get rained on. And sometimes we’re going to get pelted!
findings.note: Rain as trials that come to everyone

findings.quote: The gospel isn’t the umbrella; it’s the solid rock we’re standing on during the storm

detail.carries: the gospel holds us steady through trials, not out of them

findings.quote: When an angel asked Nephi, “Knowest thou the condescension of God?” he humbly answered,
findings.note: Nephi knows God loves him without knowing all things

detail.about: Nephi answers the angel: God loves His children, though Nephi does not know all things

findings.quote: It is precisely because He loves us that we’re having these tempering, refining experiences.
findings.note: Metal tempered and refined by heat

detail.carries: hard experience purifies and strengthens us

findings.quote: And a godlike life is carved from the very things that make it hard
findings.note: First of the carving images that close the talk

detail.carries: hardship is the material God shapes us from

findings.quote: I testify that during those sanctifying experiences, when growth is taking place and God is at work, our stories may not look like success to others.

detail.of: God is at work in hard times even when it does not look like success

findings.quote: on the outside it may look like things are sort of unraveling or falling apart
findings.note: Echoes the opening knot: what looks like unraveling is growth

detail.carries: growth can look like coming apart

findings.quote: God is shaping us into something only He knows we can become.
findings.note: A refrain, said twice in the talk

detail.carries: God forms us toward a self only He can see

findings.quote: When I spoke at Ryan’s funeral, I looked at his wife, Cari, and their four children with such a heavy heart
findings.note: Her words at her son's funeral

detail.about: at Ryan's funeral she says not understanding is not the same as not believing

findings.quote: his wife, Cari
I may not understand everything, but I absolutely believe God sees you, loves you, and knows your story
findings.note: A witness phrased as belief

detail.of: God sees, loves and knows each person's story

findings.quote: a story that is both personal and purposeful!
So you don’t need to look sideways and ask, “How come my life doesn’t look like theirs?”
findings.note: Gentle invitation not to compare lives

detail.action: stop comparing your life to others

findings.quote: It’s not a detour from the path; it gives purpose to our path.

detail.carries: suffering is part of the way, not off it

findings.quote: God is intimately aware of your experience and has a plan for all of it
findings.note: Assurance rather than conditional promise

detail.blessing: God knows your experience and has a plan for it

findings.quote: At Ryan’s funeral, his oldest son, seven-year-old Jaac, shared a Primary talk he and his dad had worked on just two weeks earlier.

detail.about: grandson Jaac's Lego talk about following God's plan and trusting the designer

findings.quote: his oldest son, seven-year-old Jaac
I love Lego bricks, and when I get a new box, I open it up and lay out all the pieces and follow the instructions.
findings.note: Lego instructions as God's plan; building without the box picture

detail.carries: follow God's plan even without seeing the finished picture

findings.quote: What would you do if you didn’t have the picture on the box, only the instructions? Would you still stick to the plan?
He answered, “Yes, because you can trust the one who designed it, and it always turns out.”
That sting is real, and that wound is wide.
findings.note: Grief for a surrendered life story

detail.carries: the real pain of losing the life you expected

findings.quote: It will take your finest faith in Christ to keep putting together the pieces—the ones that make sense but also the ones that don’t.
findings.note: Extends the Lego image to life's broken pieces

detail.carries: faith keeps building with pieces we do not understand

findings.quote: Consider this: Christ’s work in your life and His love for you are bigger than your present story.

detail.action: see Christ's work as bigger than your present story

findings.quote: And He can fix what feels badly broken.

detail.blessing: Christ can fix what feels broken

findings.quote: The day before Ryan died, he was set apart as the elders quorum president.
findings.note: Ryan's counsel to an abandoned neighbor the day before he died

detail.about: Ryan tells a deserted neighbor to turn to God and be healed

findings.quote: “Brother, you have a choice right now, and it’s a big one. You can curse God and blame Him, or you can turn to Him and let Him heal you.”
We all have a choice right now. Let’s choose Christ,
who can heal the wounds of this world while carving out room for joy!
findings.note: The blessing attached to choosing Christ

detail.blessing: healing of wounds and room for joy

findings.quote: God is saying, “Trust me,” and we are learning how to say yes.
findings.note: God's voice as she hears it, not a scripture quote

findings.quote: With an earned conviction, I witness that this—all of this—is the true and only way we can grow and progress and become like our heavenly parents and Savior.

detail.of: experience is the only way to become like heavenly parents and the Savior

findings.quote: it feels like a sort of divine mending that changes what’s happening to you into something happening for you!
findings.note: Mending answers the opening fixer image

detail.carries: God turns what happens to us into what happens for us

findings.quote: Let me leave this last visual image from a sculpting class my brother Kent took in college.

detail.about: her brother's clay self-bust comes to life only when the instructor carves it

findings.quote: my brother Kent
Our final assignment was to sculpt a bust of ourselves out of clay.
findings.note: The clay self-portrait as the soul

findings.quote: As I stepped back and looked at the piece, I could see that it was uniquely me. And yet, without a doubt, a master’s hand had shaped what mine could not.
My friends, there is sculpting taking place within each of our souls.
findings.note: The title image: Christ as sculptor of the soul

detail.carries: the Savior shapes our souls through hard experience

findings.quote: To invite the Savior to become involved is hard. Our pride gets in the way.
findings.note: Implied invitation: humble yourself and ask the Savior in

detail.action: invite the Savior to work in you

findings.quote: But as time goes on, we will begin to see the work of His hand.

detail.blessing: we will see His hand in what He carved

findings.quote: And one day, when all the suffering and loneliness have ended and our pain is gone, we will be able to step back and look into the mirror of our own soul.

detail.blessing: an end to suffering and a view of who we became

findings.quote: look into the mirror of our own soul
findings.note: Echoes Kent stepping back to see his finished bust

detail.carries: one day we will see what God made of us

findings.quote: Then we will “stand all amazed” and feel to fall at the Savior’s feet and thank Him.
We will thank Him for all of it—the molding, the shaping, the pain, and the adversity that have helped us become more like Him.

detail.purpose: what we will thank Him for

findings.quote: I joyfully testify in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
findings.note: Closing witness through 1 John 3:2: we shall see Him and be like Him

detail.of: we shall see Christ as He is and be like Him
